subject: Geo TTL & Tombstone Retention — redline questions
messages:
From: Jane Foster <jfoster@acmeretail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Retail Legal <legal@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Nov 2028 09:16:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on TTL/tombstone language in DPA

Evelyn — thanks again for the demo. Our legal and security teams dug into the DPA draft and have a couple of sticking points in the retention/deletion and residency sections before we can proceed to procurement. High level asks: 
- They want explicit language that backup copies and snapshots are subject to the same erase window and proof-of-deletion obligations.
- A requirement to certify erasure of customer records in onshore backups within 30 days unless a lawful hold is in place.
- Clarification on whether tombstoned records (soft-deletes) are retained for search/debugging telemetry and if so, for how long; they want that limited to 14 days unless agreed otherwise.
- Request for an onshore data locality guarantee for certain PII classes (contracted as a table in an appendix).

Can you confirm Redwood's position and any proposed compromise language? If useful, attaching our annotated matrix.

Thanks,
Jane Foster
Head of Cloud Security, Acme Retail

Attachments: acme_requested_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Jane Foster <jfoster@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Nov 2028 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on TTL/tombstone language in DPA

Jane — thanks, appreciated. Quick responses inline and attaching our suggested redline (Redwood_DPA_Retention_Redline_v3.pdf). Summary upfront:
- Backups & snapshots: Redwood will commit to the same erase window for production data; for immutable backups we propose a documented onshore exception process with a 45-day max cure period (can compress to 30 days for signed SLAs).
- Certification: We can provide a deletion certification within 45 days as standard, 30 days if Acme elects the Premium Erasure Add-on.
- Tombstones/soft-deletes: We generally retain soft-deleted records for 7 days for reconstruction/KV cache healing. We can extend to 14 days if explicitly requested and scoped per dataset in an appendix.
- Residency: We can commit an onshore processing lane for PII classes A/B; operationalized via a pinned model variant and geo-routing policy in the appendix.

If those concessions are acceptable I think we can close this quickly. I copied Neha (customer lead) and Marissa (security/compliance) to align on operational impacts.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Retention_Redline_v3.pdf (redline PDF)

Evelyn / Karthik — quick thoughts from Legal & Compliance: 
1) Backups: we should avoid absolute language that treats immutable backups identical to live deletion mechanics. Instead propose: "Redwood shall make commercially reasonable efforts to purge customer data from backups and immutable snapshots within the stated erase window; where technical constraints prevent immediate purge, Redwood will provide certification of logical deletion and a documented remediation schedule not to exceed X days." Set X = 45 but allow 30 with Premium Add-on.
2) Certification: 45 days standard, 30 days for paid SLA. Keep the certification scope explicit: list of systems, snapshot identifiers, and controls performed.
3) Tombstones: accept 7-day default, 14 days if Acme defines datasets in appendix. Add telemetry exemption: logs used for incident response/retention should be aggregated and pseudonymized where possible; include auditing requirement.

I'll attach a short legal paragraph to drop into the redline.

—Marissa
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal_paragraph_tombstone.txt (small stubbing)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Nov 2028 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Questions on TTL/tombstone language in DPA

Forwarding my suggested redline language for the backup clause and the tombstone paragraph. Key negotiation levers we should use: Premium Erasure Add-on (30-day commitment), Appendix table for PII classes (operationally scoped), and explicit forensic hold carveout (lawful hold).

Suggested backup clause snippet: 
"Where backups or immutable snapshots contain Customer Data, Redwood will: (a) mark such copies as logically deleted within the standard erase window; (b) provide a certification of deletion actions and identifiers within 45 days; and (c) remediate physical purging on the schedule set forth in the remediation plan, not to exceed 45 days from Customer's certified request (30 days if Premium Erasure Add-on is elected). Where a lawful hold is in effect the obligations will be tolled to the extent necessary."

Tombstone snippet: 
"Redwood may retain metadata markers (\"tombstones\") necessary for eventual recovery or KV cache consistency for a default period of seven (7) days following deletion; Customer and Redwood may elect a dataset-specific period of up to fourteen (14) days if documented in Appendix X. Any telemetry retained under this paragraph will be aggregated and pseudonymized and subject to the same deletion obligations."

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_snippets.txt

Jane — moving to commercial. We hear you on the 30-day certification requirement. Two paths to make Acme comfortable while protecting Redwood's operational constraints: 
1) Standard: 45-day certification + 7-day tombstone default (no cost)
2) Premium Erasure Add-on: 30-day certification + 14-day tombstone (scoped per appendix) + SLA credits for noncompliance.

If Acme picks option 2 we'll add the 30-day commit into Section 4 and provide a fixed-price add-on on the SOW. I'll attach a short commercial term sheet. Can we set a time next week for a quick call to finalize?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
